transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (AstraHealth CTO), Priya Varma (AstraHealth SRE), Mateo Ruiz (AstraHealth ML Eng)

Auto-generated Summary: Weekly POC sync - performance vs baseline provider, tuning items, security/QoS asks, next steps.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda, we'll run through the benchmark slides, then maya will walk the deep perf numbers, then q&a and action items.
[00:12] Jordan: yep, sounds good. we pushed yesterday's traffic into your s3 bucket, you should have the 24h slice called prod_sample_apr10.csv - let us know if you need more.
[00:20] Maya: got it, we'll pull that after. ok, first slide, high level: baseline provider vs redwood on our default 4k context model (open-llama172b-ish variant), same model family, quantization variants tested.
[00:35] Maya: so raw numbers - p50/p95/p99 latencies measured at steady-state. baseline provider p95 was ~310ms on average for the 1k input profile, redwood p95 was 240ms. throughput improved from ~95 req/s to ~125 req/s in our elastic pod config.
[00:52] Mateo: wait, are those numbers for single-node or multi-node autoscale?
[00:56] Maya: primarily single dedicated pod with continuous batching; these runs use our dedicated small pool (2x A100-equivalent). We also ran an autoscaled run - that bumped throughput to 160 req/s but with small p95 variance during scale events.
[01:10] Priya: can you clarify the workload? our traffic has a heavy tail of 30% longer sequences around 3.5k tokens, not just 1k.
[01:16] Maya: yes, good point. we ran both the 1k synthetic and a 4k mixed-profile that emulates your prod_sample. For 4k mixed, baseline p95 jumped to ~980ms while redwood p95 was ~720ms, so improvement but both higher due to KV cache invalidation and long autoregressive steps.
[01:34] Alex: to add, the 4k tail emphasizes memory and kv-cache behaviour - that's where our kernel selection and caching helps.
[01:42] Jordan: what about token throughput?
[01:45] Maya: tokens per second for mixed 4k: baseline ~22k tokens/sec aggregated, redwood ~29k tokens/sec. note this is aggregated across the pool.
[01:55] Maya: also important - cost per token estimate for these runs: baseline ~$0.000017/token, redwood ~$0.000014/token after batching benefits - that's assuming similar infra costs. we can provide granular sheets.
[02:09] Jordan: cool. one concern is p99 spike behaviour; if we have hard SLAs we need to know tail risk.
[02:16] Maya: p99 for 4k mixed: baseline ~1.8s, redwood ~1.35s in these runs. we saw p99 spikes tied to cold KV cache or background checkpointing on the provider side; our runtime mitigates with proactive prefix caching and faster KV lookups.
[02:33] Mateo: are these runs with quantized models? we tried int8 locally and saw small quality diffs but much better perf.
[02:40] Maya: we tested both fp16 and int8/4-bit quantized runs. quantization (int8) reduced p95 by ~18% on average and increased throughput by ~20%, with minimal regression on our eval set; for your prompt set we saw 1-2% accuracy delta on reranking tasks.
[02:57] Jordan: hmm, that small accuracy hit might be okay if latency improves. but need to confirm for clinical note extraction tasks.
[03:04] Alex: we can run targeted evals on your annotated subset. that's in the next steps.
[03:09] Priya: another question - how much tuning is required on our side for batching? we prefer minimal changes to client code.
[03:16] Maya: minimal. Redwood's agent supports automatic batching and adaptive timeouts; you can set a target latency SLO and the runtime auto-adjusts batch windows. There are simple flags in the client SDK, no heavy refactor.
[03:29] Speaker 2 (transcription): uh-huh, mm-hmm.
[03:33] Alex: security briefly - we did review SOC 2 scope and KMS options in the security binder. you asked about bring-your-own-KMS and SSO.
[03:42] Jordan: correct. our compliance team requires customer-managed keys, audit logs with immutability, and SAML SSO. Also need VPC peering or private link.
[03:52] Maya: we support BYOK via KMS and can route metrics and audit logs to your SIEM. For private we have a private control plane and VPC-hosted data path; on-prem deploy is also possible but takes longer.
[04:04] Priya: what's the network egress pattern for private? we need to avoid connections to public endpoints.
[04:09] Maya: private mode keeps inference traffic within your VPC, control plane can be private or customer-managed; there are options we outlined in the architecture doc. We'll demo this next week if metrics look good.
[04:20] Alex: back to perf, we noticed baseline provider had higher variance when workload had many short prefix overlaps - likely their batching is less aware of KV reuse.
[04:29] Mateo: question on cache warmup - how long until prefix/KV cache is effective?
[04:34] Maya: depends on request locality - in our tests warmup is within a few hundred requests for similar sequences; for truly unique queries warmup isn't helpful. For your prod sample, warmup reduced aggregate token work by ~12% after 10 minutes.
[04:48] Jordan: metrics are promising. one blocker is end-to-end P99 under concurrency with our auth microservices in front. any guidance?
[04:56] Maya: we recommend separate load-testing that includes your auth layer in the loop; we'll supply a load-test harness that allows you to replay sample traffic including tokenization and auth latencies. we can also run a joint load test next week.
[05:10] Alex: ok we have some tradeoff options: lower quantization for slightly higher accuracy, or faster int8 with 1-2% quality drop. Also options for dedicated vs hosted - dedicated gives more predictable throughput and isolation but has cost commit.
[05:25] Priya: for Dedicated, what are the autoscale policies and warm standby costs?
[05:31] Maya: you can configure reserved pools with burst capacity. warm standby (one extra node) is typically 15-20% of commit cost in our pricing; can be tuned. We'll include sample config.
[05:42] Jordan: compare that to baseline provider's reserved nodes?
[05:45] Maya: baseline's reserved pricing is similar but their effective throughput per node in our tests was lower, so you'd need more nodes to hit the same target. We'll share a side-by-side sheet.
[05:57] Mateo: can you share raw logs? we want to validate per-token breakdown.
[06:01] Maya: yes, we'll upload the raw perf logs and a summarized CSV of p50/p95/p99 per workload to the shared drive.
[06:08] Speaker 1 (transcription): okay, thanks
[06:12] Alex: quick callouts on tuning knobs we changed for the run: continuous batching window set to 10ms target 90ms SLO, kv cache size tuned to 12GB per model shard, kernel selection forced to fused-attn-optim path for long sequences, and mixed-quant thresholds enabled.
[06:30] Maya: one experimental thing - we tried a lightweight request coalescer that groups prefix-similar requests; this reduced duplicated kv work by ~8% in the sample. it's not GA but available for pilots.
[06:43] Priya: interesting - does that add latency for first request in a batch?
[06:47] Maya: minimal, maybe 5-8ms, since it's micro-batching at the edge; net gains for your traffic.
[06:53] Jordan: any gotchas for reranking models? we saw baseline provider have issues with beam-search memory blowup.
[06:59] Maya: redwood runtime includes memory-aware decoding paths and beam-slim heuristics; we saw 30% less memory usage on rerank workloads in our internal tests.
[07:10] Alex: question for you, Jordan - what's your target p95 SLA for this pilot to consider Dedicated?
[07:16] Jordan: ideally <500ms p95 on mixed 4k at 100 rps sustained. If we can hit that with safety margins we'd consider conversion.
[07:24] Maya: our 4k mixed p95 of ~720ms is above that today; but with quantization + coalescer + dedicated pool tuning we believe we can get below 500ms. need the extended 50k-token run to be sure.
[07:37] Mateo: timeline - how long to run the extended bench?
[07:40] Maya: 48 hours is ideal for steady-state with scale events; we can start as soon as you upload the full traffic sample.
[07:47] Jordan: we can get that to you by tomorrow.
[07:50] Alex: great. other blockers? security? procurement?
[07:54] Priya: procurement wants a standard contract; legal will need the SSO and BYOK details in the security annex.
[08:01] Alex: we'll attach our SOW and security annex to the email - I'll send the SSO/KMS integration docs and SOC 2 summary.
[08:07] Speaker 3 (transcription): okay cool
[08:09] Maya: to recap technical action items: run extended 48h benchmark (Maya), share raw perf logs (Maya), customer to upload full traffic (Jordan), Redwood to send pricing and SOW (Alex). Security follow-up: include BYOK and audit log flow in annex.
[08:25] Jordan: sounds good. one last question - did you test network jitter sensitivity? with our front-end infra we sometimes see 20-50ms jitter.
[08:33] Maya: we added client-side jitter in some runs; Redwood's adaptive batching tolerates jitter up to about 100ms without major perf regressions, but we should validate with your auth path.
[08:45] Alex: great. let's schedule the joint load test for next Tue, 2026-04-22. we'll send calendar invites after the call.
[08:53] Jordan: ok thanks all.
[08:56] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes.
